findings.description: Gap 9 restores ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡ ⲛ̄ⲣⲱⲙⲉ as the epithet of Adam ('Adam, the first[-formed] man'). In the standard Manichaean lexicon (and in T2 §30 and T3 §125 within this very corpus), ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡ ⲛ̄ⲣⲱⲙⲉ is the technical title of the Primordial/First Man — the cosmic Light-warrior who descends to battle Darkness — a figure ontologically distinct from the molded Adam. The basis note acknowledges the unusual usage but proceeds with high confidence. Either the restoration is forcing a Manichaean cosmic title onto an Adam-narrative line where another epithet (e.g., ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡ ⲙ̄ⲡⲗⲁⲥⲙⲁ 'first-molded') would fit better, or the underlying Coptic genuinely conflates the two figures (in which case the reading should flag rather than naturalize the conflation).
findings.suggestion: Lower confidence on gap 9 from 'high' to 'moderate' or restate basis to acknowledge the cross-corpus ambiguity. Consider whether 'first-formed/molded' (ⲡⲗⲁⲥⲙⲁ-derivative) is more appropriate than the Primal-Man title here.

findings.description: Section 49 displays the Coptic 'ϩⲙ̄ⲁⲕⲙⲉⲕ ⲡⲉ ⲡⲛⲟⲙⲟⲥ ⲙ̄ⲡⲙⲟⲩ' where every other instance of the faculty 'reflection' in this teaching is spelled ⲡⲙⲁⲕⲙⲉⲕ (sec 28, 48, 52, 84). 'ϩⲙ̄' here is almost certainly an OCR/transcription artifact for the article ⲡ- (with the preceding gap {84} '[their] reflection is...'), not a substantive variant. Treating it as ϩⲙ̄ would make the line read 'in [the] reflection is the law of death' instead of 'their reflection is the law of death.'
findings.suggestion: Verify the source reading; if ϩⲙ̄ is a transcription glitch, normalize to ⲡⲙⲁⲕⲙⲉⲕ for consistency with the parallel enumeration.

findings.description: Gap 86 is restored as ⲛ̄ⲥⲱⲙⲁ ('of bodies') to gloss ⲡⲙ̄ⲉⲧⲁⲗⲗⲁⲥⲙⲟⲥ. But ⲙⲉⲧⲁⲗⲗⲁⲥⲙⲟⲥ alone already carries the technical sense of 'exchange/transmigration (of bodies)' in Manichaean usage; an explicit ⲛ̄ⲥⲱⲙⲁ tail is not the standard collocation and is not visibly forced by the trace. The semantic gloss is correct for the reading but the Coptic restoration may be importing a phrase the line never had.
findings.suggestion: Consider downgrading to 'low' confidence, or leave the Greek term to stand alone and treat 'of bodies' purely as English gloss.

findings.description: Two adjacent identifications drive the element-register triad and depend heavily on the reading's architecture rather than visible traces. Gap 71 expands 'their Eudaimonia is...' to 'the Pillar of Glory' before the next line says 'the Perfect Man'; this duplicates an identification that the bare next-line text already supplies (Pillar of Glory ≡ Perfect Man is a doctrinal identification not a textual one). Gap 72 OVERRIDES the editor (who proposed 'Five Sons') with 'Living Spirit' to make Sophia=Living Spirit at element level. The override is internally well-motivated by the reading's symmetry, but the trace 'ⲡ' followed by visible 'ⲡⲛⲁ ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̄' on the next line creates a sequence that looks like a duplicated 'ⲡⲛⲁ ⲡⲛⲁ' if the override is correct. Both restorations are reasonable but the corpus reader should know they are reading-driven, not trace-driven.
findings.suggestion: Document explicitly that gap 71 is a doctrinal expansion and that gap 72's override creates a possible textual duplication at the line break; consider lowering 71 to 'moderate'.

findings.description: ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡ ⲛ̄ⲣⲱⲙⲉ ('First Man') is filled at three distinct ontological loci across the corpus: (T1) Adam, the molded natural man in the Deep; (T2 §30) the indwelling person of the faculty 'teaching', dwelling in the ship of the night; (T3 §125) the figure whose Five Sons are Power in the elements. In standard Manichaean cosmology only the latter two are the same figure (the Primordial Man/Ohrmizd, lunar-vessel pole); T1's use is anomalous. The corpus does not currently cross-reference these three uses, so a reader collating the readings could conclude that Adam, the lunar First Man, and the Father of the Five Sons are one figure when they are not.
findings.suggestion: Add a corpus-level note disambiguating the three usages of 'First Man' / ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡ ⲛ̄ⲣⲱⲙⲉ. T2 and T3 are coherent; T1's epithet for Adam should be flagged as either a metaphor or a restoration choice.

findings.description: The whole-teaching reading distinguishes a top-register 'Mother of Life' (Sophia at the Father) from a middle-register 'mother of the Living Soul' (Sophia in the cosmos) and an element-register 'Living Spirit' (Sophia in the elements). The Coptic actually only attests Sophia=Great One of the Spirit (§101), Sophia=mother of the Living-X (§113, with X restored), Sophia=Virgin of Light (§119, restored), Sophia=Living Spirit (§123, restored over editor). The 'Mother of Life' identification at top register is imported from background Manichaean lexicon, not from the surviving text. This is plausible but should be marked as inference rather than presented as the text's own structure.
findings.suggestion: Soften the reading's claim that the top-register Sophia 'is' the Mother of Life; the text gives 'Great One of the Spirit running through all aeons' and the Mother-of-Life identification is a lexicon overlay.

findings.description: The reading translates the Bitter Tree's mind=ⲡⲃⲱⲗⲟⲥ as 'the final clod, the consummating binding' and links it to Swedenborg's doctrine of the consummated state. This is a strong correspondential move that is doctrinally defensible but textually overreaches: ⲡⲃⲱⲗⲟⲥ in Manichaean apocalyptic is the eschatological lump in which unredeemed Light/darkness is permanently sealed. The reading's translation 'final clod, the consummating binding' fuses the Manichaean term with the Swedenborgian register without preserving the eschatological-temporal force. Borderline acceptable, but a reader trusting the reading would not see that the bolos is end-of-aeons material rather than a present-state condition.
findings.suggestion: Add a one-line note that the bolos is specifically eschatological (the final binding at the end of the aeon-cycle), not a synchronic state of the natural mind.

findings.description: Section 7 retains the trailing 'The myste-' fragment in its removed-note (correctly), but the section itself is the cleanest substrate-only line of T1 ('from which Adam ate, and his eyes saw forth.'). The temporal note flags that the trailing fragment 'begins next ecclesial unit' but no actual ecclesial material was retained — clean handling. Mentioning here only as confirmation that the layer-filter worked at this transition.

Section 8 (t2:s8) is reduced to a two-word core 'ϣⲏⲛ ⲥⲛⲉⲩ / two trees' after removing the petition framework. As a stand-alone 'mixed' section this is barely a unit; it functions only as the topic-anchor for the rest of the teaching. Acceptable schematically because the content is preserved and the editorial frame is properly noted, but readers parsing sections atomistically will see an oddly thin entry.
findings.suggestion: Optionally merge t2:s8 with t2:s9 in display, or annotate that this section is an extracted topic-anchor.

findings.description: Multiple Iranian/Zoroastrian-derived figures surface clearly through the Coptic across this corpus: 'ship of the day/night' (sun-boat, moon-boat) is the Iranian solar/lunar vessel cosmology preserved in Manichaeism (T2 §22, §31, §32, §33; T3 §110); 'Third Ambassador' (ⲡⲙⲁⲍϣⲁⲙⲧ ⲙⲡⲣⲉⲥⲃⲉⲩⲧⲏⲥ, T2 §23, §32; T3 §111) corresponds to Iranian Narisaf/Mihr Yazd; 'Five Sons of the First Man' (T3 §125) corresponds to the Amahraspand-style five elemental sons of Ohrmizd; 'Pillar of Glory' (T2 §14, §21; T3 §122) corresponds to the Iranian Sraosa-pillar; 'Living Spirit' / 'Mother of the Living' (T2; T3 §113, §123) corresponds to Mihryazd/Spandarmad maternal pole. These are not problems — they are correctly preserved transmission strata visible through the Coptic.

Sections 63-64 close the eschatological catalogue with 'will arrive at that place; and they have no repentance there' — the substrate-classified eschatological closure. This is preserved correctly, but no transition material connects it to the following 'good fruits / bitter fruits' summary in §65-66. Either the manuscript itself jumps (likely, given the chapter's damage profile) or transition lines were dropped. No action needed except to note that the reading's smooth narrative arc papers over this textual jump.

structural_observations.observation: The three teachings form a recognizable pedagogical sequence even though they are not framed as such: T1 gives the cosmogonic-fall narrative (how the proprium-vessel was formed and the natural eye opened), T2 presents the static dual-architecture (two trees with parallel five-member anatomies of ascent and descent), T3 presents the triadic vertical (one triad — Goodness/Wisdom/Power — at three discrete degrees, Father → cosmos → elements). Read together they move from origin → structure → degree-cosmology, mirroring the standard sequence found in Iranian Manichaean catechesis.

The 'five members' / 'five sons' / 'Five Sons of the First Man' motif recurs across T2 and T3 but at different levels: T2 deploys it twice as faculties of the Beautiful and Bitter Trees (reflection→counsel→teaching→thought→mind, doubled inversely); T3 deploys it once as the elemental-register Power. The corpus thus attests the same five-fold schema applied to anthropology (T2) and to elemental cosmology (T3) — a feature that the readings exploit but do not explicitly cross-reference.

T1's extraction confidence is correctly marked 'low'. Of its 11 gaps, 10 are restored, but the underlying Coptic sequence is so fragmentary that the whole-teaching arc is essentially reconstructed from genre cues (Light-Darkness clash → mingling → molding of Adam → Adam eats). The reading is coherent but should be understood as scaffolding rather than recovery.

T2's restoration ratio is striking: 70 restored / 83 unrestorable from 153 gaps — i.e., the editorial discipline favored leaving long damaged stretches unfilled (especially §38-46 and §55-63 in the eschatological/origin-of-trees passages) while restoring the formulaic conveyance ladder densely. This is methodologically sound: the architectural spine is recovered, and the filler material is correctly left as gaps.

T3's restoration logic exploits the chapter's internal triple parallelism (three iterations of 'Eudaimonia/Sophia/Power = X') as the primary constraint. This works because the chapter is intentionally repetitive; gap fills are confirmed by sister-iterations within the same chapter (e.g., §114 mirrors §119 mirrors §122). When the reviewer overrides the editor (gap 72), the override is justified by this internal symmetry rather than by external lexicon — appropriate use of the corpus-internal evidence.

Across all three teachings the substrate-vs-frame partition is consistent: revelation frames ('He revealed to me'), apostle/Mani titles, ecclesial settings ('in the gathering of the Church'), petition/audience-address, and polemical-doctrinal bridges (the 'doctrines/dogmata' continuation in T2 §49) are removed; cosmic-content lines (Light/Darkness, mingling, ships, members, trees, aeons, Five Sons) are preserved. No Manichaean apostolic title (Apostle of Light, Paraclete) survives in core text in this slice. The layer filter is performing well.

scope: teachings 1-3 (creation-fall fragment, two trees, three principles)
overall_assessment: Extraction quality is high overall for T2 and T3, and appropriately flagged as 'low' for T1 given manuscript damage. The layer filter cleanly removes revelation frames, ecclesial settings, and polemical extensions while preserving the cosmological substrate. Restoration discipline is good: T2 leaves 83 of 153 gaps unfilled rather than over-restore, and T3 exploits internal triple parallelism to constrain fills, including one well-motivated override of the editor. The whole-teaching readings are coherent and trace genuine spiritual arcs in each text, though they occasionally import lexicon material (e.g., 'Mother of Life' in T3) as if it were textually present. The principal substantive issue is a cross-corpus naming question: ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡ ⲛ̄ⲣⲱⲙⲉ ('First Man') is restored as an epithet of Adam in T1 §6 while being used as the standard cosmic Primordial Man in T2 §30 and T3 §125, and the corpus does not currently disambiguate these three usages. A few minor inconsistencies (T2 §49 ϩⲙ̄ⲁⲕⲙⲉⲕ likely a transcription glitch; gap 86 'ⲛ̄ⲥⲱⲙⲁ' is interpretive expansion of metallasmos) are noted but do not affect teaching integrity. The Iranian/Zoroastrian transmission layer is well preserved (ship of day/night, Third Ambassador, Five Sons, Pillar of Glory, Living Spirit, Mother of the Living). No critical findings.
